bullets.title: SPCX beat-and-raise is the dominant AI capex signal: 13GW by YE27, $35-40B Q4 capex
bullets.body: SpaceX Q3 revenue came in at $14.6B vs $12.8B consensus (+161% YoY), with Super Intelligence segment profitable for the first time. Management raised 2026 nameplate compute guidance to 2.5-3GW and targets 13GW by YE27 with 20GW upside; Q4 capex guided to $35-40B vs $20B consensus. Sub-1-year payback periods and investment-grade financing ($35-60B quarterly capacity) make demand signals credible — bottleneck has shifted from chips to power/cooling.

bullets.title: SMCI pre-announces Q1 revenue $18.5-19.5B, 27% above prior guidance; margins expand
bullets.body: Super Micro raised preliminary FQ1 revenue to $18.5-19.5B from $14.5-15.5B on AI platform demand and mix shift; gross margin guided to 12.0-12.5% vs prior 10.4-10.8% guidance and consensus 10.4%. Stock +12.3% pre-market; bullish read-through for DELL (+6.8%) and HPE (+4.5%) on server infrastructure spend continuing to accelerate.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler capex cycle accelerating to ~$1.5T in 2027; equity-credit dislocation a warning sign
bullets.body: MS estimates aggregate hyperscaler data center capex at ~$900B in 2026, growing ~60% YoY to ~$1.5T in 2027; META guided 2027 capex at $225-250B vs $201B consensus. Despite equity rallies of 5-7%, AI-linked CDS spreads widened sharply (ORCL 350bps, AVGO 160bps), suggesting positioning-driven equity move rather than fundamental confirmation. ~30GW of new compute expected operational in 2027; execution risk and power/cooling remain primary bottlenecks.

bullets.title: NFLX -7% on Q4 revenue guide miss and ad shortfall; multiple converging toward traditional media
bullets.body: Netflix Q3 beat on revenue and EPS but Q4 guide disappointed; FY2026 advertising revenue outlook cut from $3B to $2.7B on third-party integration delays and slower US engagement. FY FCF guide trimmed from $12.5B to ~$12B. Stock trading at 14x GIR CY28 GAAP EPS vs DIS at 15x, with multiples converging toward legacy media — stock near 2-year lows and ~50% off ATHs.

bullets.title: Macro regime: US Quad 2 (growth + rising rates); 10-year at 5.10%, VIX 16.6
bullets.body: Hedgeye maintains Quad 2 (growth accelerating, inflation rising) for October with 83% conviction on Quad 2 in December. US 10-year yield sits at 5.10% — Hedgeye's TRADE signal level — with risk range 5.06%-5.33%; Treasury shorts (TLT, zero-coupon) maintained. VIX at 16.61 with the 17.5 level flagged as key TRADE resistance; SPX gamma flip at 7,726 with S&P futures +0.34%.

bullets.title: Hedgeye rotates out of QQQ into equal-weight and healthcare; software exposure cut to 6%
bullets.body: Keith McCullough sold the remainder of QQQ and rotated into DJIA, RSP, XLV, and HTEC; Microsoft, Apple, and Amazon all moved to bullish TRADE and TREND. Software exposure reduced to ~6% minimum (IGV, BUG, XLK each ~2%). QQQ TRADE resistance at 737, TREND support at 721 — signal is bearish TRADE but bullish TREND vs. equal-weight bullish on both dimensions.

bullets.title: AT&T beats Q3 but shares -7% on SpaceX wireless entry threat in 2028
bullets.body: AT&T raised FY26 adjusted EPS guidance to ~$2.40 (from $2.25-$2.35), maintained $18B+ FCF, and reduced 2027-28 annual capex to $22-23B; fiber net adds of 442K beat consensus 379K. Despite the operational beat, shares fell ~7% after SpaceX confirmed plans to enter US wireless in 2028, raising competitive structure concerns and weighing on VZ (-3.2%) in sympathy.

bullets.title: AI-yields correlation turned positive; market views AI capex as growth story, not inflation
bullets.body: Positive correlation has emerged between AI buildout beneficiary stocks and Treasury yields, as investors interpret AI capex as a growth driver rather than an inflationary force. 10-year breakevens locked at 2.25%; a plateau in AI capex would imply only 40-50bps GDP drag. Consumer expenditure at 3%+ remains the primary growth driver — AI capex a secondary but forward-looking factor for long-end yields.

bullets.title: AI infrastructure skeptics: ~50% of US AI chips reportedly unused; financing stress widening
bullets.body: Bears argue roughly 50% of deployed AI chips sit idle due to data center construction delays, and Nvidia may be pressuring customers to accept GPUs before installation capacity exists. Widening CDS spreads for CoreWeave and Oracle reflect financing scrutiny, with Anthropic described as showing slowing revenue growth and substantial losses. Hedgeye flags CoreWeave as an active short on financing risk.

bullets.title: GOOGL: Pichai says frontier AI is #1 priority; compute for 2027 'extremely difficult' to secure
bullets.body: Google CEO Sundar Pichai confirmed frontier model development is the company's top priority, with the firm deliberately forgoing near-term revenue to invest in compute R&D. Compute capacity constraints for 2027 described as severe. Gemini 4 Argon hit ~25T tokens in first 72 hours (~3x Gemini 3); Google preparing persistent autonomous consumer agents spanning Gemini, Search, Gmail, and Workspace.

bullets.title: META reports tonight; 2027 capex guided $225-250B; Muse AI app 10M downloads in 40 days
bullets.body: META Q4 revenue guided at $75B high end vs $74B consensus; 2027 capex projected at $225-250B, well above $201B consensus. Muse AI app reached 10M US downloads in 40 days with better retention than competing products. Q3 revenues expected >25% YoY; Reels, messaging, and AI monetization are key discussion items for tonight's call.

bullets.title: Data center political risk rising: 30GW of 2028-30 deliveries exposed to midterm outcomes
bullets.body: Jefferies estimates 30GW (34% of total projected 2028-30 deliveries) are at risk from state-level election outcomes in TX, GA, and OH on November 3; Texas alone accounts for ~26% of nationwide exposure. Opposition to data centers surged from 42% to 75% in one year across both parties. NIMBYism favors incumbents DLR and EQIX by widening mark-to-market spreads; HPC developers with secured power better positioned than those awaiting conditional ERCOT approvals.

bullets.title: TSLA-SPCX merger: special committees formed, $100-150B equity raise priced in
bullets.body: Elon Musk confirmed Tesla and SpaceX formed special committees to evaluate a merger; 22V notes a $100-150B equity raise is being priced in ahead of expectations. TSLA investor focus has shifted away from margins and capex toward Cybercab deployment timelines and FSD v15 progress.

bullets.title: OCC finalizes GENIUS Act stablecoin rules effective Jan-27; digital assets going mainstream
bullets.body: OCC issued final rules implementing the GENIUS Act for payment stablecoin issuance by regulated entities, establishing reserve backing, redemption, risk management, and supervisory frameworks effective January 2027. UBS launched a ~50-slide Digital Asset Strategy report characterizing the impact on Payments/FinTech, Banks, Exchanges, and Asset Managers as neutral-to-moderately positive, with tokenized real-world assets estimated at $88T by 2035.

bullets.title: SMCI AI infrastructure rally lifts data center power/cooling complex; VRT +6%, BE in focus
bullets.body: SMCI's pre-announcement and SPCX's capex raise drove broad gains across AI infrastructure: VRT +6%, with Wolfe noting VRT configures AI factory designs 10x faster with 30% token output improvement. Bloom Energy in focus ahead of earnings as CCUS integration with data center fuel cell exhaust (95% CO2 profile vs 5% for engines) offers cost-neutral emissions reduction, with Oracle Project Jupiter cited as evidence.

bullets.title: US hotel RevPAR +5.5% for week ended 10/17; midscale leads, Las Vegas down 13%
bullets.body: US RevPAR grew 5.5% YoY to $126 (ADR +2.3%, occupancy +3.1%) — a slight deceleration from +6.5% the prior week. Midscale chain-scale outperformed at +8.0% while luxury trailed at +1.2%; Las Vegas was the worst single market at -13.2% YoY. Group RevPAR on a 4-week average was +12.4%, supporting a still-intact Q4 lodging setup.

bullets.title: Architecture billings declined in September; leads construction spend by ~6 months
bullets.body: The AIA Architecture Billings Index fell to 44.7 from 47.2, remaining in contraction territory amid soft economy, challenging project financing, and client caution. Only Commercial & Industrial billings moved into expansion; Midwest and West regions expanded while Northeast and South contracted. Because billings lead construction spending by roughly six months, the reading flags potential softness in early-2027 construction activity.

bullets.title: Cybersecurity stocks rallying on AI-discovered critical PHP bug affecting 70% of websites
bullets.body: Reports that an AI tool identified one of the most severe PHP vulnerabilities on record — affecting up to 70% of the world's websites — drove a broad rally in cybersecurity names on urgency around patching and proactive defense spending.

bullets.title: Mortgage applications -5.3% WoW; 30-year rate slipped to 7.41% from 7.50%
bullets.body: Mortgage applications fell 5.3% for the week of 10/16 despite a modest 9bp decline in 30-year rates to 7.41%. Refi mix held at 39% vs 61% purchase. EFX has ~20% revenue exposure to mortgage; FICO mortgage ~20% of revenue — recent EFX results expected to ease near-term mortgage concern.

bullets.title: Financials earnings: beats driven by below-the-line items, not operational strength
bullets.body: JPM flags that broad financials beats this quarter — including COF's $1.19 EPS upside and SYF's provision-driven beat — reflect lower charge-offs, reserve releases, and tax rate tailwinds rather than core operating improvement. MCO missed with MIS revenue -1% YoY on weak leveraged finance issuance; Moody's macro assumptions turned cautious with spec-grade default rate raised to 3.8% and HY spreads to 300bps. XLF trending from bearish toward potentially bullish but JPM sees insufficient clean operational beats to attract new buyers.
